description: Triage-only candidate list from BugsInPy — NOT yet verified with ESBMC. Phase 2 (later) will write harnesses and verify each with `esbmc --z3`.
source: BugsInPy (Widyasari et al., ESEC/FSE 2020) — peer-reviewed dataset of real bug-fixing commits in open-source Python projects

already_confirmed_in_dataset.note: already in dataset as av_real_04 (being reworked per Fernanda's feedback)

candidates.bug_description: Uses undefined/wrong variable `output_path` instead of `output` when opening the output file (NameError/AttributeError).
candidates.justification: Single-line wrong-variable-reference bug; trivially isolable as a tiny function taking a string path.
candidates.filter_reason: Real bug is get_write_function() referencing undefined name `output_path` instead of `output` -- fails at ESBMC conversion time (NameError-style, unresolved identifier), not a VCC-based counterexample. Confirmed by direct probe in a prior pass.

candidates.bug_description: `responses` dict merge crashes when the caller's `responses` param is None (no guard before `{**responses, **route.responses}`).
candidates.justification: Isolable as a 2-arg dict-merge function with Optional[dict] input.
candidates.filter_reason: Optional[dict] merge (responses = {**responses, **route.responses}); pure dict-merge logic, dict literals/update fully supported by ESBMC-Python. No stubbing needed beyond the two dict inputs.

candidates.bug_description: Host/netloc parsing via string `find('/')`/slicing produces wrong netloc when host segment present in the URI.
candidates.justification: Pure string index/slice logic once extracted from Sanic app/config context.

candidates.bug_description: `self.app.config.SERVER_NAME` accessed without guarding for AttributeError when config attr absent.
candidates.justification: Isolable as a function taking an Optional config object/flag.

candidates.bug_description: `int(head) - 1 if head != "0"` fails to also guard the CoNLL-U `_` sentinel, causing a wrong index / ValueError on int("_").
candidates.justification: Pure string/int scalar function, no external deps at all.

candidates.bug_description: Sort key `(span.end-span.start, span.start)` should use `-span.start`; wrong tie-break order causes wrong span selected as longest/first.
candidates.justification: Isolable as sort over list of (start,end) int tuples.
candidates.filter_reason: Fix is a lambda sort key (span.end-span.start, -span.start) used as sorted()'s key= argument. sorted()/list.sort() with a custom key is NOT listed anywhere in src/python-frontend/README.md's Features Supported (no sorted()/.sort() builtin at all in the Built-in Functions section) -- real unsupported-feature risk, not just a stubbing question.

candidates.bug_description: Uses `is not -1` (identity compare on ints, CPython small-int-cache gotcha) instead of `!=`, plus double `.pop()` on `command.script_parts`.
candidates.justification: Pure list/int logic; classic Python identity-vs-equality gotcha, no external deps.
candidates.filter_reason: Real fix adds --set-upstream/-u stripping via list.index()+pop(), then joins script_parts. list.index() is NOT in ESBMC-Python's supported list-method set (only append/extend/insert/clear/pop/remove/copy per README Limitations) -- needs a manual scan-loop rewrite instead of .index(), which is a legitimate adaptation, not a blocker. Separately, the `is not -1` int-identity check inside the (already-fixed) code is a genuinely interesting open question -- whether ESBMC-Python models `is` on int literals like CPython's small-int cache -- worth a dedicated probe once ESBMC runs resume, independent of whether this candidate is accepted.

candidates.bug_description: `machine=None` default later string-concatenated (`"vagrant up " + machine`), TypeError when machine is None.
candidates.justification: Trivial string+None concat bug.
candidates.filter_reason: Not a None-crash: pre-fix default was `machine = ""`, not None. Wrong-output bug about the 'start all instances' case, mislabeled by triage. Confirmed by a prior full-patch read.

candidates.bug_description: Missing `__bool__`/`__nonzero__`; before the fix, `if tqdm_instance:` used default object truthiness (always True) instead of total/iterable-based truthiness.
candidates.justification: Needs a small class stub with total/iterable attrs; truthiness semantics testable via assert.
candidates.filter_reason: Adds __bool__/__nonzero__ dunder methods to tqdm class. Whether `bool(x)` on a plain object actually dispatches to a user-defined __bool__ in ESBMC-Python is undocumented in README's OOP/Limitations sections. Not confirmed unsupported -- needs a direct probe (a tiny class with __bool__ under `if obj:`) once ESBMC runs resume, before committing to a harness.

candidates.bug_description: `total` computed from `len(iterable)` only after other init logic already used the old (unset) `total`; ordering bug, already an open lead from a prior mining pass.
candidates.justification: Isolable as an ordering/assignment bug on Optional[int] total.

candidates.bug_description: `self.total` accessed directly instead of `getattr(self, "total", None)`, AttributeError if `total` not yet set on the instance.
candidates.justification: Simple attribute-presence bug, trivial to isolate.

candidates.bug_description: Rounding-boundary bug: `abs(num) < 1000.0/100.0/10.0` should be `999.95/99.95/9.995` (values that round up to the next unit at the boundary print wrong, e.g. "1000.0K" instead of "1.0M"). Same commit also touches a `len(self.iterable) if self.iterable else self.total` None-fallback in `__len__`.
candidates.justification: format_sizeof is a pure numeric scalar function, very isolable; the __len__ fallback is a second, separate none_misuse-shaped bug in the same patch.
candidates.filter_reason: Real, dependency-free SI-unit rounding bug in format_sizeof -- already confirmed genuine in a prior pass, but timed out at 60s / 286 VCCs even narrowed to one branch. Not a support limitation, a solver-performance one -- retry with a longer timeout or narrower float encoding when ESBMC runs resume.

candidates.bug_description: `__gt__` defined as `not self.__lt__(other)` (wrong: this equals "not less than", which includes equality, so gt returns True on equal values) instead of `not self.__le__(other)`.
candidates.justification: Comparison-operator logic bug; isolable with a minimal stub class exposing __lt__/__le__/__eq__ over an int-like ordinal.

candidates.bug_description: Removes every key in `to_remove` unconditionally, even if the same key is also present in `to_set` (should skip keys still being set).
candidates.justification: Pure dict/list membership logic, two dict/list params, no external deps.

candidates.bug_description: `before -= self.previous_after` computed even when `self.previous_line is None` (start of file), yielding a wrong/negative empty-line count instead of 0.
candidates.justification: Core arithmetic is scalar; needs a thin stub for previous_line/previous_after state.
candidates.filter_reason: Previously mis-assessed as not fitting an assert-on-crash shape. Reconsidered: fits the buggy-function/correct-function equality-assert pattern already proven for matplotlib/24 (av_real_09) and others -- `before = before - self.previous_after` (buggy) vs `before = 0 if self.previous_line is None else before - self.previous_after` (correct) is pure int+bool logic, no crash needed, ESBMC finds the diverging input (previous_line is None) via the pair-assert technique.

candidates.bug_description: `table in stdout` substring check is case-sensitive; Hive normalizes table names to lowercase, so real (differently-cased) tables are reported as not existing.
candidates.justification: Trivial string membership/case bug, fully self-contained.

candidates.bug_description: try/finally sets `status` unconditionally to DONE-path logic even when new_deps indicates SUSPENDED, because the original code relied on a finally block that didn't check the branch taken.
candidates.justification: Isolable as a small state-machine function (new_deps: Optional[list] -> status enum), medium stubbing needed for Task/logger/event calls.
candidates.filter_reason: try/finally restructure: status becomes DONE vs SUSPENDED depending on whether new_deps is None. Core logic isolable as Optional[list] -> status-enum-int function; self.task.trigger_event/logger/json.dumps calls need light stubbing (side-effect calls, not decision-relevant).

candidates.bug_description: When `linewidths` is an iterable containing None entries, those entries are not replaced by the rcParam default (only the whole-None case was handled).
candidates.justification: List[Optional[float]] substitution logic; needs stubbing rcParams default as a plain float.
candidates.filter_reason: linewidths is None-or-list branch, `np.iterable(linewidths)` narrows to a plain `isinstance(linewidths, list)` check without loss of the bug shape. Recommend narrowing the harness's type to `list[float] | None` (drop the scalar-linewidth case) to avoid ESBMC-Python's Union-widening limitation across more than two shapes.

candidates.bug_description: Order-of-checks bug: `positions is None or len(positions) == 0` computed after other operations already assumed non-None, or before proper validation, allowing a later crash on None.
candidates.justification: Isolable as an Optional[list] validation function.
candidates.filter_reason: Re-investigated beyond the diff hunk (was previously just deferred): the actual fix is about `positions` needing `.ndim`/`.size`, which pre-fix only worked via `hasattr(positions, 'ndim')` because plain lists lack `.ndim` -- inherently about numpy ndarray semantics (np.array conversion, .ndim, .size), not isolable to pure Python types. Confirms the original numpy-coupling rejection, now with the concrete reason.

candidates.bug_description: `allowed_domains` list may contain `None` entries; regex `.match(domain)` crashes (or is filtered inconsistently) if a None domain isn't skipped before pattern matching.
candidates.justification: Pure list-filter-with-None-check logic once separated from the regex-building context.

candidates.bug_description: No `url is None` check before use; the fix adds `raise ValueError("url can't be None")`.
candidates.justification: Single added None-guard, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Missing mutual-exclusivity check: previously both `response` and `text` could be passed together silently; fix raises ValueError if both are non-None.
candidates.justification: Pure two-argument None/None logic, fully self-contained.

candidates.bug_description: `'Basic ' + creds` string+bytes concatenation raises TypeError once `creds` becomes bytes (b64encode result) in Python 3.
candidates.justification: Needs ESBMC bytes support confirmed; str/bytes concat is the whole bug.

candidates.bug_description: `objcls.from_crawler(...)` (or `from_settings`/`__new__`) may legitimately return None (misbehaving extension); previously this propagated silently instead of raising `TypeError`.
candidates.justification: Isolable as a function returning Optional[object] then checked; needs light stubbing of the dynamic dispatch.

candidates.bug_description: URL-scheme check `':' not in self._url` is too loose (matches Windows paths like `C:\...` as having a scheme); fixed to check for `'://'` plus a `data:` exception.
candidates.justification: Pure string-membership/startswith logic, fully self-contained.

candidates.bug_description: Header-dict condition only checked `"Transfer-Encoding" not in headers`, missing the case where it's present but equal to "chunked" (should still be treated as absent for this check).
candidates.justification: Pure dict membership + string-equality logic.

candidates.bug_description: No `args is None` early return; previously passing `None` for `args` reached code that assumed an iterable/mapping and crashed.
candidates.justification: One-line None-guard, extremely simple to isolate.

candidates.bug_description: Inverted boolean condition: `is None` used where `is not None` was intended (or vice versa) when checking whether a current IOLoop instance already exists.
candidates.justification: Classic inverted-condition bug; needs a bool flag standing in for the singleton-instance-exists state.

candidates.bug_description: Filter-lambdas `'': lambda v: v is not None` / `'!': lambda v: v is None` don't special-case bool values, so a False value is treated as "is not None" (True) under the '' filter, which is semantically wrong for a boolean field.
candidates.justification: Pure bool/None branching logic in two one-line lambdas.

candidates.bug_description: Return type inconsistency: `return 0.0` (falsy-but-not-None float) changed to `return` (None) to make a "no match" result unambiguous from a real numeric filter result of 0.0.
candidates.justification: Small function; needs the call site's truthiness check included in the harness for the bug to matter.
candidates.filter_reason: Re-investigated: real crash is `para.attrib['begin']` raising KeyError when the 'begin' attribute is absent from a dfxp/TTML paragraph dict -- dict subscript KeyError is natively checked by ESBMC-Python (README: 'raises KeyError if absent'), so this reproduces near-verbatim with a plain dict literal missing the key, same technique as oob_real_04/05. Mislabeled as type_mismatch by triage -- recategorize as out_of_bounds or a new key_error-shaped category, not type_mismatch.

candidates.bug_description: `if int_str is None: return None` checked the wrong condition; fixed to `if not isinstance(int_str, compat_str): return int_str`.
candidates.justification: Entire function is 3 lines, fully self-contained, no deps.

candidates.bug_description: `compat_chr(int(numstr, base))` raises ValueError for numeric character references outside the valid Unicode range; no guard existed before the fix.
candidates.justification: Pure int/chr scalar logic, fully self-contained.

candidates.source_function: limit_length (new function, extracted from facebook.py inline logic)
candidates.bug_description: Inline title-truncation logic didn't guard against `s is None`, and used a fixed offset (`+3`) instead of accounting for the ellipsis length correctly.
candidates.justification: The fix literally extracts a clean, tiny, self-contained function - almost zero adaptation needed for a harness.

candidates.bug_description: No check that `start_index <= end_index`; also an off-by-one in `(end_index - start_index)` (should be `+ 1`, inclusive range) causing wrong length/out-of-range sampling.
candidates.justification: Pure int arithmetic/comparison, core logic has no tensor/numpy dependency.

candidates.bug_description: `isinstance(x, list)` branch didn't handle `x is None or len(x) == 0` ("data tensors", no explicit input) before falling through to list-specific logic.
candidates.justification: Isolable as an Optional[list] branch-selection function.
candidates.filter_reason: Rejected for numpy/tensor-internal coupling in a prior pass (`.ndim`/tensor `.shape` involved) -- confirmed, not re-investigated further.

candidates.bug_description: List comprehension `[v if i > v else v - 1 for v in clocs]` uses the wrong loop variable `i` (a leftover/typo) instead of the intended threshold `val`, producing wrong index remapping.
candidates.justification: Pure list-of-int remapping logic once separated from the MultiIndex context; classic wrong-variable bug.

candidates.bug_description: `columns` argument not checked for None before use; fixed to raise `TypeError("pivot() missing 1 required argument: 'columns'")`.
candidates.justification: Single added None-check, trivially isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: Re-investigated beyond the diff hunk (was previously deferred as needing pandas-internal context): the fix itself is just `if columns is None: raise TypeError(...)` guarding pivot()'s entry -- does NOT require tracing into pandas' actual pivot/reshape internals. Fits the buggy-function/correct-function precondition-pair pattern already proven for ip_real_11 (fastapi/12): model `columns_is_none: bool` nondet input, buggy_raises=False (always), correct_raises=columns_is_none, assert equal -- ESBMC finds the divergence. No pandas dependency needed at all. Reverses the prior rejection.

candidates.bug_description: String-slice prefix stripping (`command.script[5:]`) instead of proper prefix replace produces wrong URL when script isn't exactly 'open '-prefixed.
candidates.justification: Pure string slicing/concat, trivially isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: `'open http://' + command.script[5:]` (assumes exactly 5-char 'open ' prefix) vs `command.script.replace('open ', 'open http://')` -- pure string slicing/replace logic, isolable as a plain str function, no external deps.

candidates.bug_description: `.format()` appends '--staged' as new token instead of inserting after 'diff', producing malformed command string.
candidates.justification: Pure string formatting, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Calls `self.fs.mkdir(d)` where `self.fs` doesn't exist on this class; should be `self.mkdir(d)` (AttributeError).
candidates.justification: Needs a minimal stub class with a real mkdir method vs a missing fs attribute; low complexity but not pure-scalar.

candidates.bug_description: Checks `'Host' not in headers` against a freshly-built dict (always true) instead of `self._orig.headers`, always overwriting Host.
candidates.justification: Pure dict membership-check logic once isolated, two dict args.
candidates.filter_reason: Diff alone shows `headers = dict(self._orig.headers)` immediately followed by the changed check -- `'Host' not in headers` vs `'Host' not in self._orig.headers` are checking equivalent dicts at that point unless something mutates `headers` in between that isn't shown in the hunk. Could not confirm a real observable divergence from the patch context alone; would need the full surrounding function body to rule in or out, not attempted further given time budget.

candidates.bug_description: Drops `str()` coercion (`self._label = label` instead of `str(label)`), so a non-str label silently changes the attribute's type.
candidates.justification: Single-line type-coercion removal, trivially isolable as a scalar function.
candidates.filter_reason: Re-investigated (was previously deferred citing 'Any-type limitation'): `self._label = str(label)` -> `self._label = label` removes a forced str() coercion, so `label` is genuinely polymorphic (str or not) across the buggy/correct boundary. This is really a Union-widening issue, not exactly Any-type: README's Union Type Limitations say Union types are 'resolved to the widest type among their members at verification time rather than maintaining true union semantics' -- so comparing a coerced-to-str value against an uncoerced original value across that boundary isn't representable with real None/type-preserving semantics. Confirms the prior deferral as a real limitation, with a more precise citation.

candidates.bug_description: Substring check `'ls' in command.script` matches any command containing 'ls' (e.g. 'als'); should require an exact/prefix match.
candidates.justification: Pure string membership/prefix boolean logic.

candidates.bug_description: Substring check `' -s ' in command.script` misses '-s' at the end of the command (no trailing space).
candidates.justification: Pure string membership boolean logic.
candidates.filter_reason: `"php -s" in command.script` vs `" -s " in command.script` -- pure string containment check, isolable, no external deps.

candidates.bug_description: Missing early-return guard for commands already starting with 'sudo', causing double-sudo suggestions.
candidates.justification: List/string check on script_parts[0], isolable with a list input.
candidates.filter_reason: Adds an early-return guard on `command.script_parts[0] == 'sudo'` before the existing stderr/stdout pattern scan -- list indexing + string membership, both natively supported, isolable as list[str]+str.

candidates.bug_description: Substring check `'set-upstream' in command.output` too loose; should require the full 'git push --set-upstream' phrase.
candidates.justification: Pure string membership boolean logic.
candidates.filter_reason: `'set-upstream' in command.output` vs `'git push --set-upstream' in command.output` -- pure string containment, isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Appends the whole `extrabuf` instead of only its last `extrasize` bytes, corrupting decompressed output.
candidates.justification: Bytes/str slicing with negative index, supported by ESBMC's slicing.
candidates.filter_reason: output += f.extrabuf[-f.extrasize:] -- bytes slicing with a negative start index. README confirms negative-index slicing is supported for str, and the scrapy/23 rejection established ESBMC-Python treats bytes like str internally for basic operations, so slicing (not concatenation, which is what broke scrapy/23) is plausible. Flag the bytes-as-str caveat for whoever verifies next.

candidates.bug_description: Doesn't verify the matched file path actually exists before suggesting a fix, unlike the fixed version's `os.path.isfile` guard.
candidates.justification: Isolable with `os.path.isfile` stubbed as nondet_bool, matching os module's nondeterministic modeling pattern.
candidates.filter_reason: Adds `os.path.isfile(m.group('file'))` check. `os.path.isfile` is NOT in ESBMC-Python's supported os-module function list (only exists/basename/makedirs/mkdir/rmdir/listdir/remove/popen per README) -- but the established convention elsewhere in this dataset is to stub external filesystem state as a bare `nondet_bool()` standing in for the file-exists outcome, same as os.path.exists is modeled nondeterministically. Legitimate abstraction, not a blocker.

candidates.bug_description: Calls `self.s3_load_path()` as a method when it's actually a property, raising TypeError ('str' object is not callable).
candidates.justification: Needs a minimal class stub with a property vs a plain attribute; moderate confidence given ESBMC's property/descriptor support is unconfirmed.
candidates.filter_reason: Bug is calling a @property as if it were a method (self.s3_load_path() vs self.s3_load_path). Whether ESBMC-Python's class support extends to the @property descriptor protocol isn't stated either way in README's Features Supported or Limitations sections -- needs an actual esbmc run to resolve, can't be settled by reading docs alone.

candidates.bug_description: `dict.pop(netloc)` removes the key entirely instead of setting it to None, so later lookups raise KeyError instead of getting None.
candidates.justification: Pure dict operations (pop vs subscript-assign), isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: self._parsers.pop(netloc) (removes key) vs self._parsers[netloc] = None (keeps key, sets value). Pure dict pop/subscript-assign, both supported. Needs a minimal stub for rp_dfd.callback(None) (a Deferred-like object with a callback method).

candidates.bug_description: Calls `len(self.columns)` without checking `self.columns` isn't None first, raising TypeError when unset.
candidates.justification: Minimal None-guard-before-len bug, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Missing `config.update(overrides)` means caller-supplied overrides are silently dropped from the pipeline component config.
candidates.justification: Pure dict-merge logic, isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: config.update(overrides) -- dict.update() is a supported dict operation, isolable as a 2-dict merge function.

candidates.bug_description: Calls `compat_str(upload_date)` unconditionally even when `upload_date` is still None, returning the literal string 'None' instead of None.
candidates.justification: Scalar None-vs-value coercion logic, isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: Adds `if upload_date is not None:` guard before `return compat_str(upload_date)`, else implicit None. Not a crash (`compat_str(None)` just yields the string "None", no exception) -- a wrong-value bug (returns literal string "None" instead of Python None on the failure path). Fits the buggy/correct pair-assert pattern. Caution: use an explicit if/else to assign the None case, NOT a ternary -- README already documents that a ternary assigning None to a str-annotated variable does not preserve NULL semantics in ESBMC-Python (found while building nm_real_03).

candidates.bug_description: Lambda `lambda attr, value: not str_op` negates the (always-truthy) function object instead of calling `str_op(attr, value)`, always evaluating False.
candidates.justification: Lambda/callable-truthiness bug; ESBMC's lambda support is basic (naive return-type inference), so this needs a probe before committing.
candidates.filter_reason: `lambda attr, value: not str_op` (bug: negates the function object itself, always False) vs `not str_op(attr, value)` (calls it). Modeling this needs a lambda that invokes another callable captured from an enclosing scope (STR_OPERATORS[...]) -- this is higher-order/closure-capturing lambda usage, which README's Limitations section explicitly excludes ('Higher-order and nested lambda expressions are not supported'). Real risk, not attempted.

candidates.bug_description: Drops the `if params[param_name].significant:` guard, serializing non-significant parameters that should be excluded.
candidates.justification: Needs a dict-of-objects (or dict of bool flags) stub for Parameter.significant; moderate complexity.
candidates.filter_reason: params[param_name].significant guard dropped. Isolable with a small stub class (Parameter: significant: bool, serialize(x) -> value) held in a dict; supported via ESBMC-Python's class/attribute/dict support.

candidates.bug_description: Calls `_pipe(pipe, docs, kwargs)` with arguments in the wrong order (should be `_pipe(docs, pipe, kwargs)`).
candidates.justification: Classic swapped-argument bug; needs `_pipe`'s real signature/semantics to build a faithful harness.
candidates.filter_reason: Bug is a swapped-argument call to _pipe(pipe, docs, kwargs) vs _pipe(docs, pipe, kwargs); _pipe's real signature/semantics aren't in this diff hunk or anywhere nearby -- building a harness would mean inventing _pipe's behavior, not reproducing the real bug faithfully.

candidates.bug_description: Builds the merged dict starting from `self` then applying `kwargs` (self wins), when `kwargs` should take precedence over existing settings.
candidates.justification: Pure dict.update() ordering bug, cleanly isolable with two dict literals.

candidates.bug_description: `while len(self) >= self.limit` compares int to None when `limit` isn't set, raising TypeError (Python 3 disallows int/None ordering).
candidates.justification: Reduces to an int-vs-Optional[int] comparison, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Builds `exc_info` tuple in the wrong order `(value, type, tb)` instead of Python's `(type, value, tb)` convention.
candidates.justification: Pure tuple-construction/ordering bug, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Splits PATH on hardcoded `:` instead of `os.pathsep`, breaking on non-POSIX path separators.
candidates.justification: String split logic; low confidence since `os.pathsep` support in ESBMC's os model is unconfirmed.
candidates.filter_reason: `.split(':')` vs `.split(os.pathsep)` -- fundamentally a platform-dependent separator bug (os.pathsep differs by host OS), not a logic bug ESBMC's environment model would disagree with CPython on. Also depends on `Path(path).iterdir()`, real filesystem iteration far beyond ESBMC's tiny modeled os-function surface. Already low confidence in triage; confirmed not isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Only strips 3 keys (`_type,url,ie_key`) from `force_properties` instead of the full set, leaking stale keys (e.g. `id`) into merged results.
candidates.justification: Pure tuple/dict-key-deletion logic, isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: Tuple of dict keys to delete extended from 3 to 6 entries -- pure dict+tuple key-deletion logic over a fixed key set, isolable as a wrong-value (missing-deletion) bug via the buggy/correct pair pattern.

candidates.bug_description: Default arg `last_active=None` combined with downstream numeric comparisons/arithmetic can raise TypeError when no timestamp is passed.
candidates.justification: Needs the downstream comparison code (not in this hunk) to build a faithful harness; moderate confidence.
candidates.filter_reason: Diff hunk only shows a default-arg change (last_active=None -> last_active=time.time()); the actual downstream comparison/arithmetic that would crash on None isn't in this hunk or visible nearby -- insufficient context to build a faithful harness, same trap as other 'need more context than the diff hunk shows' rejections.

candidates.bug_description: Swaps which extra bound feeds `max()` vs `min()` (`oldmax` should pair with `min()`, `oldmin` with `max()`), producing wrong axis limits.
candidates.justification: Pure scalar min/max logic; needs 2-arg chained min/max since ESBMC only supports 2-arg min/max (real code uses 3-arg).

candidates.bug_description: Tab characters advance the column counter by 1 instead of 4, miscounting indentation width.
candidates.justification: Pure char-loop/int-counter logic over a string, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: `assistant or worker in task.workers` short-circuits truthily for any assistant call, ignoring whether the task actually has workers; operator-precedence/logic bug.
candidates.justification: Boolean + list-membership logic, isolable with a bool and a list input.
candidates.filter_reason: assistant or worker in task.workers -> (assistant and task.workers) or worker in task.workers -- pure bool + list-membership (`in`) logic over primitives, fully supported.

candidates.bug_description: Case-sensitive `headers.get("Transfer-Encoding") == "chunked"` misses `Chunked`/`CHUNKED`, silently skipping chunked-body parsing.
candidates.justification: Pure dict.get + string-equality logic, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Hardcodes `self._filled = True` instead of deriving it from `self._fillstyle != 'none'`, so unfilled markers are wrongly marked filled.
candidates.justification: Single-line string-comparison-to-bool bug, trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Tuple membership check omits UNKNOWN status and uses `getattr(...,None)` instead of direct attribute access, changing which tasks count as necessary.
candidates.justification: Tuple-membership + attribute-presence logic over string status constants, isolable.
candidates.filter_reason: Tuple-membership check (task.status not in (DONE, DISABLED[, UNKNOWN])) plus getattr(...,None) vs direct attribute access. Isolable with a small stub Task class (status: str, scheduler_disable_time: Optional); tuple `in` and attribute access both supported.

candidates.bug_description: Indexes `command.script.split()[1]` without checking the split list has at least 2 elements, raising IndexError on short commands.
candidates.justification: Classic list-index-without-length-check bug, minimal and clean.

candidates.bug_description: Indexes `self._cached[0]` without checking `self._cached` is non-empty, raising IndexError.
candidates.justification: Classic list-truthiness-before-indexing bug, minimal and clean.

candidates.bug_description: Missing float conversion before `abs()`/subtraction lets fixed-width integer types wrap around (e.g. `abs(int8(-128)) == -128`), causing spurious overflow.
candidates.justification: Currently 0 items in this category; needs verifying whether ESBMC-Python's plain `int` has bounded/wrapping semantics like the real numpy int8 case, or whether the bug only manifests with a numpy dtype stub.
candidates.filter_reason: Already confirmed in a prior pass by direct probe: `np.int8(-128)` scalar constructor is unsupported (`ERROR: Unsupported NumPy function call: int8`).

candidates.bug_description: `to_bytes(parsed.hostname)` with `hostname=None` isn't guarded, unlike the fixed `parsed.hostname or b''`.
candidates.justification: Minimal None-guard-before-conversion bug, isolable with a string/bytes stand-in for to_bytes.
candidates.filter_reason: to_bytes(parsed.hostname) vs to_bytes(parsed.hostname or b'') -- classic None-guard-before-conversion, same shape as other confirmed none_misuse items. Needs a light stub for to_bytes (str/bytes passthrough, raises on None).

candidates.bug_description: Always raises on a non-bearer scheme instead of respecting the `auto_error=False` flag (should return None silently).
candidates.justification: Pure bool-flag-controlled branching (raise vs return None), trivially isolable.

candidates.bug_description: Indexes `src_txt[-1]` on a possibly-empty string, raising IndexError; fixed version uses slice `src_txt[-1:]` instead.
candidates.justification: Classic empty-string index-vs-slice bug, minimal and clean.

candidates.bug_description: Formats stale `l_bar`/`r_bar` variables instead of the freshly-split `l_bar_user`/`r_bar_user`, using outdated format strings.
candidates.justification: Wrong-variable-reference bug, isolable as two string variables and a pick-the-right-one function.

candidates.bug_description: Calls `configure_http_handler` on the wrong object (`metrics`, the generated payload) instead of `metrics_collector` (the object that actually defines that method).
candidates.justification: Wrong-object-reference bug (AttributeError-shaped), isolable with two minimal stub objects.
candidates.filter_reason: Wrong-object-reference bug: metrics.configure_http_handler(self) called on the payload object instead of metrics_collector (the object that actually defines that method). Isolable with two minimal stub classes -- one with the method, one without -- an AttributeError-shaped bug ESBMC-Python's exception hierarchy covers.

candidates.description: Conditional dropped 'and not needs_update(vrf)' guard, so a state+vrf update together only applies the state change when vrf does NOT also need updating -- pure bool-logic bug.
to/cc accepted as a bare string (not wrapped in a list) get joined char-by-char via COMMASPACE.join(to); fix wraps via arg_to_iter(). Isolable string-vs-list join bug.
settings.get('SPIDER_LOADER_CLASS', settings.get('SPIDER_MANAGER_CLASS')) precedence swapped vs intended (deprecated key should be the fallback, not the primary). Pure dict.get() precedence bug.

`if self._instance_cache.get(self.io_loop) is not self: raise RuntimeError(...)` fires a false RuntimeError when the cached value is None (weakref cleared) instead of only when it's a different real instance. Pure dict/None identity-logic bug.
Linked-list unlink does `current_line.next.prev = current_line.prev` unconditionally; crashes with AttributeError when current_line.next is None (removing the tail node). Fix adds a None-guard.

HTTP range check `(start is not None and start >= size) or end == 0` doesn't catch an inverted/invalid range (start >= end); also negative-start clamping happened after the satisfiability check instead of before. Pure int/bool range-arithmetic bug.

Re-scheduling guard checked only `task.status in (RUNNING, BATCH_RUNNING) and status == PENDING`, allowing a different worker to bump a running task back to PENDING; fix adds `task.worker_running != worker_id`. Isolable as bool/enum-int state check across a handful of status constants.
candidates.filter_reason: Re-scheduling guard: adds `(status not in (DONE, FAILED, RUNNING) or task.worker_running != worker_id)` to the condition. Pure bool/string-constant/tuple-membership logic over a handful of status values, fully supported types.

candidates.description: Swapped `max(vmin,vmax,oldmax)`/`min(vmin,vmax,oldmin)` args (should be oldmin/oldmax matched to max/min respectively). Real code uses 3-arg min/max -- ESBMC-Python's min()/max() only support 2 args per src/python-frontend/README.md Limitations, so the harness must rewrite as nested 2-arg calls (max(max(a,b),c)), a modeling deviation to note in abstraction_notes.
candidates.filter_reason: Swapped args: `max(vmin,vmax,oldmax)`/`min(vmin,vmax,oldmin)` (buggy) should be `max(vmin,vmax,oldmin)`/`min(vmin,vmax,oldmax)` (correct). Same shape as the already-confirmed av_real_09 (matplotlib/24), which already proved the 2-arg-nesting workaround for ESBMC-Python's 2-argument-only max()/min() (nested `max(max(a,b),c)`). High confidence given the directly analogous, already-proven precedent.

candidates.description: `http.RESPONSES.get(int(status))` has no default, so an unknown status code yields None fed into to_native_str(None); fix adds a default 'Unknown Status'. Uncertain whether to_native_str(None) actually raises in ESBMC's str model or just stringifies -- needs a probe before trusting this as a crash-shaped bug.
candidates.caveat: unverified whether to_native_str(None)-equivalent actually raises under ESBMC; probe before harnessing
candidates.filter_reason: http.RESPONSES.get(int(status)) with no default vs .get(int(status), 'Unknown Status') -- dict.get() with/without default, to_native_str() of the result. All supported constructs (dict.get, int(), str conversion). Triage's own caveat (whether to_native_str(None)-equivalent actually raises under ESBMC) is an empirical question for the esbmc run, not a doc-level limitation -- keep the caveat attached for that step.

candidates.description: `abs(vmin)`/`abs(vmax)` on integer types can wrap around (e.g. numpy int8 abs(-128)==-128) before the fix adds `map(float, [vmin, vmax])`. Real trigger needs numpy fixed-width int wraparound semantics -- ESBMC-Python's plain int type likely doesn't reproduce this the same way (per README, numpy dtype-specific behavior isn't in the modeled subset). Low confidence this reproduces as-is.
candidates.limitation_flag: needs numpy int8 wraparound semantics, likely unsupported
candidates.filter_reason: Identical underlying patch to matplotlib/16 (same np.int8/np.abs issue) -- same rejection, already confirmed.

candidates.description: When job.jar() is None, code still reaches `os.path.abspath(job.jar())` in the error-logging path, crashing with TypeError; fix raises a clean HadoopJarJobError first. `os.path.abspath` is NOT in ESBMC-Python's supported os-module function list (only exists/basename/makedirs/mkdir/rmdir/listdir/remove/popen per README) -- likely unsupported, low confidence.
candidates.limitation_flag: needs os.path.abspath, not in supported os function list
candidates.filter_reason: Confirmed real ESBMC-Python limitation: the crash path is os.path.abspath(job.jar()), and os.path.abspath is NOT in src/python-frontend/README.md's supported os-module function list (only exists/basename/makedirs/mkdir/rmdir/listdir/remove/popen are modeled). Matches the triage's own limitation_flag.

candidates.description: Missing bytes-to-str coercion on `path`/`base` before the isinstance(compat_str) check, so a bytes input silently returns None instead of joining. ESBMC-Python treats bytes as str internally (known gotcha from scrapy/23 in the prior pass) so the isinstance/decode dance may not model the real crash path -- low confidence.
candidates.limitation_flag: bytes handling ambiguous in ESBMC-Python per known scrapy/23 finding
candidates.filter_reason: Bug is about bytes-vs-str handling in urljoin (`isinstance(path, bytes)` then `.decode('utf-8')`). Matches the already-documented scrapy/23 finding: ESBMC-Python treats `bytes` as `str` internally, so a bytes/str type-mismatch bug like this one isn't faithfully representable -- confirmed same limitation, not re-tested independently given the direct precedent.

candidates.bug_description: Off-by-one bound check: guarded l[i+4] access with 'i+3 < len_l' instead of 'i+4 < len_l', causing IndexError on a specific timestring shape.
candidates.justification: Clean scalar/list index-bound bug, isolable without any dateutil-specific types -- just a list-of-tokens and an integer index.

candidates.bug_description: list_of_lists[0] accessed unconditionally to compute num_cols; IndexError when list_of_lists is empty. Real GitHub issue #180, has a regression test.
candidates.justification: Verbatim-isolable: a function taking a list of lists and indexing [0] without an empty check.

candidates.bug_description: _type(string) called _isint(string) etc. on a None value without a None check first, raising TypeError. Fixed by returning the text type immediately when string is None.
candidates.justification: Tiny scalar function, easily isolable, real GitHub issue #1.

candidates.bug_description: '%' format operator applied to retry_state.seconds_since_start, which can be None (when outcome_timestamp is unset), raising TypeError. Fixed with a None guard falling back to '?'.
candidates.justification: Isolable to a scalar float-or-None input and a format-string operation; real GitHub issue #591, has a regression test.

candidates.bug_description: simple_separated_format() built a TableFormat with headerrow=None; when actually printing headers this crashes with TypeError instead of the data row format being reused. Real GitHub issue #15.
candidates.justification: Depends on the TableFormat namedtuple structure used elsewhere in tabulate.py -- needs to check how much of TableFormat's consumer code is isolable before committing.

candidates.bug_description: format(float(raw_val), floatfmt) crashes with ValueError/TypeError when raw_val doesn't actually convert to float (e.g. bool-like strings); now caught and falls back to str(val).
candidates.justification: Scalar string-to-float conversion crash, should isolate cleanly to a small function.

candidates.bug_description: __get__(self, obj, objtype=None) assumed obj is never None, but class-level attribute access (e.g. autospec inspection) passes obj=None, causing incorrect wrapper replacement.
candidates.justification: Relies on Python's descriptor protocol (__get__ invoked by attribute access machinery) -- ESBMC-Python's class/instance model may not trigger __get__ the way CPython does; needs a probe before committing.

candidates.bug_description: Fallback max-timestamp constant used Dec 31 which overflows datetime.timestamp() on 32-bit systems; changed to Jan 1 of the same year.
candidates.justification: Bug is about datetime.timestamp() overflow behavior differing by platform/word-size -- ESBMC-Python's datetime model may not reproduce 32-bit overflow semantics at all; needs a probe, likely not isolable as a generic scalar bug.

candidates.bug_description: When count is None and factor==1.0, count is inferred via math.log(stop/denom, factor); math.log(x, 1.0) divides by zero (log(1.0)==0), raising ZeroDivisionError instead of a clear error.
candidates.justification: Clean scalar bug: a float division inside math.log(x, base) with base=1.0. Isolable without any boltons-specific types, just start/stop/factor floats.

candidates.bug_description: Negative index normalization ran twice (once in __getitem__, once in _get_real_index), so an out-of-range negative index like x[-n-k] silently wrapped to a wrong in-range element instead of raising IndexError.
candidates.justification: Isolable double-offset arithmetic bug on a list-like index; needs an assert comparing expected IndexError/wrong-element behavior rather than a direct crash, since the buggy version returns a wrong value, not a crash.

candidates.bug_description: float(not_parsed)/float(num_substrings) and a second similar division both crash with ZeroDivisionError when num_substrings is 0.
candidates.justification: Clean scalar division bug over two int counters; a second genuine division_by_zero case outside matplotlib, which the dataset's README flagged as scarce in BugsInPy.

candidates.bug_description: os.path.isfile(v)/os.path.isdir(v)/os.path.exists(v) called directly on v without a None guard; real os.path functions raise TypeError on None instead of returning a validator-friendly False/exception.
candidates.justification: Fixes #204. Model as a nondet bool standing in for 'v is None' rather than calling the real os.path function, matching the dataset's existing none_misuse pattern (nm_real_01/02).

candidates.bug_description: `skey` is only assigned inside the inner `for skey, svalue in s.items(): ...` loop; when the schema dict `s` is empty, the loop body never runs and a later reference to `skey` raises UnboundLocalError.
candidates.justification: Same shape as the existing variable_misuse item (vm_real_01/tqdm_8): a variable referenced after a loop that may execute zero times. Isolable to a dict-iteration scalar model.

candidates.bug_description: '%r' % k crashes with TypeError when k happens to be a tuple, because the % operator unpacks a tuple RHS into multiple format args instead of treating it as one value; fixed by wrapping as '%r' % (k,).
candidates.justification: Fixes #50. Minimal, fully isolable repro: a single %-formatting expression whose behavior depends on the runtime type (tuple vs scalar) of one value.

candidates.bug_description: self[key] == that[key] is evaluated for every key in self without first checking key in that, raising KeyError when that is missing a key self has (e.g. comparing to a plain dict of different shape).
candidates.justification: Same buggy-vs-correct-pair pattern already used for invalid_precondition items: the real fix adds the missing 'key in that' guard before indexing.

candidates.bug_description: end was set directly to the caller-supplied n; when n exceeds len(pwcs) the loop indexes past the string end, raising IndexError. Fix clamps end = min(n, len(pwcs)).
candidates.justification: Fixes #228, has a regression test. Clean scalar/string-length bound bug, minimal to isolate.

candidates.bug_description: num.endswith(decimal) is called unconditionally; when the caller passes decimal=None (to disable decimal-word substitution), str.endswith(None) raises TypeError.
candidates.justification: Clean, isolable: a single str.endswith() call whose argument may be None depending on a caller flag. Matches the dataset's existing none_misuse shape.

candidates.bug_description: x[0] is accessed unconditionally at the top of both functions; called with an empty string (which natsort's own regex splitting can produce), this raises IndexError.
candidates.justification: Minimal, fully isolable: a single str[0] access guarded only by an 'if not x' check added in the fix. Real user-triggerable bug (issue-linked, has regression test).

candidates.description: `len(other.indexes > 1)` evaluates the comparison `other.indexes > 1` (a list vs int) before len() is even called -- raises TypeError('>' not supported between instances of 'list' and 'int') whenever this branch is reached, fixed to `len(other.indexes) > 1`.
candidates.notes: Deterministic crash on that branch, not input-dependent -- isolable as a small function taking a list and doing the same buggy comparison shape.

candidates.description: `obj.append(_guess_type(elements, elem, index), next_element)` calls list.append() with 2 positional arguments -- TypeError: append() takes exactly one argument (2 given). Fixed by moving next_element inside the _guess_type(...) call.
candidates.notes: obj is guaranteed a list at this point via the preceding isinstance(obj, list) check -- isolable as list.append(x, y) misuse.

candidates.description: Function builds a `matches` list, then only `return self.__class__(matches)` inside `if matches:` -- when matches is empty, falls through with no else, implicitly returning None instead of an empty list. Real GitHub issue #18.
candidates.notes: Classic missing-else-branch None-return bug, cleanly isolable to a small function; assert result == [] vs None.

candidates.description: `H += 12` for PM times with no upper-bound check -- if H was already 12 (12 PM), H becomes 24, and datetime(...) raises ValueError('hour must be in 0..23'). Real GitHub issue #16. Fix adds `if H > 23: day_incr = True; H -= 24`.
candidates.notes: Isolable as an H-computation function with assert 0 <= H <= 23 -- medium confidence since it depends on whether ESBMC-Python's datetime model (src/python-frontend/models/datetime.py) actually validates the hour range the same way CPython does; needs a probe.

candidates.bug_description: In the ZWJ (zero-width-joiner) branch, `result[-1]` is accessed with no check that `result` is non-empty, and `string[i-1]` is accessed with no check that `i>0`. A malformed string starting with a ZWJ triggers IndexError.
candidates.justification: Minimal, isolable: two unguarded index accesses in a char-by-char loop, fixed by adding `result and` / `i > 0` guards. Real issue #263, has regression test.

candidates.bug_description: After preprocessing, an empty `paths` list is passed straight into the Windows-specific batch-delete pipeline (mbcs conversion, full-path resolution) instead of returning early, crashing on an operation that assumes at least one path.
candidates.justification: Real issue #71, has regression test. Needs the exact downstream crash point (past what the diff hunk shows) confirmed in phase 2 before modeling as a buggy/correct pair.

candidates.bug_description: `full_path.replace(dest_dir_path, src_dir_path)` replaces ALL occurrences of dest_dir_path in the string, not just the leading prefix. If the directory name recurs deeper in the path, sub-paths get silently corrupted to the wrong value instead of just renaming the prefix.
candidates.justification: Clean scalar string-logic bug, no I/O needed once os.walk's output is modeled as an input list. Real issue #1158, has regression test with a concrete corrupting example. Wrong-value bug (not a crash) -- model as buggy-str.replace() vs correct-slicing pair with an assert on the expected result, same pattern as the math.gamma pi_const fix.

candidates.bug_description: When `filename` has no '.', `filename[::-1].find('.')` returns -1, so `name = filename[:-1*(-1)-1]` evaluates to `filename[:0]` -- silently truncates the filename to empty instead of using the whole string. Fix adds an explicit branch for the no-extension case.
candidates.justification: Pure string-index-arithmetic bug, no external deps. Wrong-value bug, not a crash -- model as buggy-vs-correct name-computation pair with an assert.

candidates.bug_description: `dotenv_values(file)` can return `None` for a variable declared without a value (e.g. `FOO=` in a .env file). Before the fix, every value -- including None ones -- was passed through `to_env()` unfiltered, crashing when a variable has no value.
candidates.justification: Real issue, fix adds `if v is not None` filter to a dict comprehension. Needs `to_env()`'s exact implementation checked in phase 2 (not found at current HEAD path, may have moved) to model the crash faithfully.

candidates.description: H/0 style hash cron field (e.g. '* * H/0 * *') computes `(crc >> idx) % (range_end - range_begin + 1)` with a zero-width range, raising ZeroDivisionError instead of a clean CroniterBadCronError.
candidates.issue_ref: no issue number in commit message, but has a dedicated regression test (test_invalid_divisor)

candidates.description: `dt.month % step` returns 0 (an invalid month) whenever dt.month is an exact multiple of step (e.g. month=6, step=3); fix is `((dt.month - 1) % step) + 1` to stay in the valid 1-12 range. Pure int arithmetic, isolable without datetime.
candidates.issue_ref: PR #235, has a dedicated regression test (test_expand_from_start_time_month_divisible)

candidates.description: `tuple(filter(None, self.to_tuple()[index]))` uses Python truthiness, so a legitimately-zero version part (e.g. patch=0) gets filtered out like a missing part, corrupting slice/index results instead of raising the intended IndexError only for truly-absent parts.

`_parse_uname_content(lines)` indexes `lines[0]` without checking for an empty list, raising IndexError when `uname -rs` produces no output. Pure function on `Sequence[str]`, no subprocess/OS dependency at this level -- near-verbatim isolable.

phase1_continuation_note: Second triage pass (widened net): read patches for 150 additional pre-unfiltered bugs across all 18 projects (beyond the original 172), plus revisited projects previously low-yield in the first pass. 39 new candidates accepted, bringing the total from 37 to 76. Did not exhaust the source: roughly 300+ BugsInPy Python bugs remain unread (pandas is the bulk of what remains and has a documented low yield). Headroom still exists for a third pass if more candidates are wanted.
phase1_round3_note: Round 3 (direct execution, not a sub-fork): cross-referenced existing 76 candidates + 30 confirmed dataset items + README-mentioned rejections against ~399 unread BugsInPy bugs, sorted by patch size, manually read the smallest ~195 non-pandas/non-keras patches (pandas/keras deprioritized per prior passes' low yield: 2/83 and low respectively). Found 12 new candidates. Each cross-checked against src/python-frontend/README.md's Limitations section per explicit instruction after phase-2 verification on the first 37 caught misses (scrapy/23 bytes-as-str, youtube-dl/11 needing re.sub, a sanic bug needing deque) that a limitations check would have flagged at triage time -- 5 of these 12 are flagged medium/low confidence for exactly this reason (3-arg min/max, os.path.abspath not in the supported os function list, numpy int8 wraparound semantics, bytes/str ambiguity) rather than silently included. ~200 non-pandas/keras patches remain fully unread, plus ~200 pandas/keras patches barely spot-checked -- not exhausted, but full manual reading at this scale is expensive; a further pass could add more.
phase1_round4_note: Round 4: read all 189 remaining non-pandas/non-keras/non-cookiecutter/non-PySnooper BugsInPy patches (the full tail after rounds 1-3), sorted smallest-first, in full. Zero new candidates accepted. Systematic finding: this remaining tail is dominated by framework-internal state (matplotlib rendering/axes internals, scrapy/tornado/fastapi networking and pydantic model internals, ansible system-facts/galaxy plugins, black/blib2to3 parser internals, luigi scheduler Task-object state, youtube-dl extractor-specific HTML/JS scraping) that cannot be isolated to a scalar/list/dict/str core without stubbing so much of the real object graph that the harness would no longer test the real bug. A second recurring pattern: several small thefuck patches (bug 6, 12, 13) loosen or tighten a shell-command match() guard (substring/which() checks) -- same shape as the already-rejected thefuck/15 documented in the original README Findings ("loosens a match guard, does not fix a crash") -- these do not raise an exception or produce a checkable wrong value, they just change which shell-correction suggestion fires, so they were rejected for the same reason, not included as new candidates despite superficial simplicity. Remaining headroom for a future pass: pandas (~168 patches never fully read; historical yield 2 confirmed of ~85 read) and keras (~43 patches never fully read; historical yield 2 of ~47 read) are the only unexhausted pools, both previously deprioritized for low yield -- reading them fully would be the only way to push meaningfully past the current 88 candidates from this source.
phase1_fresh_github_mining_note: One-shot worker pass (coordinator's spend limit forced this to run inline, not as a sub-fork). BugsInPy pandas/keras remainder read in full for the first 80 (of 160) smallest pandas patches and all 43 unread keras patches -- 0 new candidates, 100% internal Index/ExtensionArray/dtype/Tensor/Layer machinery, confirming and extending the established low-yield pattern (did not read the remaining 80 pandas patches given this consistent 0% hit rate). Then mined 9 fresh GitHub projects beyond BugsInPy's 18 (click, rich, arrow, pendulum, dateutil, python-tabulate, more-itertools, cachetools, tenacity) via `git log --grep=fix` + full diff read of matches referencing a GitHub issue number -- 8 new candidates, 6 high/medium confidence (dateutil, python-tabulate x4, tenacity), 2 low-confidence flagged for a support probe before harness-writing (cachetools' __get__ descriptor protocol invocation, arrow's platform-dependent datetime overflow). click, rich, pendulum, more-itertools yielded nothing on this pass (mostly type-annotation-only fixes or test-only fixes, e.g. more-itertools' numeric_range_zero_step commit only touched the test file, not source).
phase1_batch2_fresh_github_note: One-shot worker pass (ran inline, not as a sub-fork, per coordinator instruction after the previous fork hit the account's spend limit). Cloned 24 new small/pure Python libraries beyond the 9 already tried (boltons, chardet, marshmallow, python-slugify, voluptuous, natsort, schema, humanfriendly, attrs, w2n, python-ftfy, python-email-validator, python-phonenumbers, python-titlecase, unidecode, wcwidth, inflect, parsimonious, parsedatetime, python-sortedcontainers, dateparser, charset_normalizer, validators, toolz). Fixed the search command from the prior pass's docs (a combined '-iE' flag string silently matched 0 commits everywhere -- git requires the two flags separated, '-i -E'; with that fixed, 15/24 projects had real hits). Read every 'fix'-grep hit with an issue-number reference or a clear crash-type in the message across boltons, dateparser, voluptuous, schema, sortedcontainers, wcwidth, inflect, and natsort (marshmallow/chardet/charset_normalizer/validators/toolz/email_validator/parsedatetime/ftfy/phonenumbers/attrs had hits but yielded either library-internal encoding-table dependencies (charset_normalizer's iana_name lookup), platform-dependent behavior (toolz's 32-bit OverflowError), Python-2-only bugs (email_validator's UnboundLocalError, out of scope per the 'skip pure Py2/3 compat' rule), or regex-pattern changes too deep in re-module semantics for ESBMC-Python's limited re support (parsedatetime's lookahead fix) -- none accepted from those). 10 new candidates: 2 real division_by_zero cases (boltons' math.log(x,1.0), dateparser's search.py rating division -- the second real division_by_zero find outside matplotlib, which BugsInPy's own corpus never yielded), 3 out_of_bounds, 2 none_misuse, 1 variable_misuse (same shape as the existing tqdm_8 item), 1 type_mismatch, 1 invalid_precondition. Cloned repos cleaned up from /tmp/newmine2 after mining. No esbmc run, no harness .py files written, no ground_truths touched, per the coordinator's mid-session correction to stay in phase-1 candidate-gathering only.
phase1_fresh_github_mining_setA_note: Set-A fresh-GitHub-projects pass (run by a fork nested inside the mining coordinator). Cloned 14 small/pure libraries (Box, blessed, colorama, deepdiff, dictdiffer, fuzzywuzzy, glom, jmespath.py, jsonpath-ng, jsonschema, parse, termcolor, toml, tomli) with corrected `-i -E` grep flags. 4 accepted after full-diff read (2 deepdiff type_mismatch, 1 jmespath none_misuse, 1 parse invalid_precondition-medium). Rejected without a harness: colorama's win32 API bugs (not Python-logic, platform API calls), colorama's atexit None-guard (module teardown semantics, not representable), jsonpath-ng's isinstance(bool)-shadowed-by-isinstance(int) bug (real but needs an explicit assert to be checkable, not a natural crash -- left for a future pass), jsonpath-ng's negative-indexing lexer change (feature add, not a bug fix), most jsonschema/glom/dictdiffer/fuzzywuzzy/termcolor/toml/tomli/Box/blessed hits were type-hint-only, merge commits, or version-bump commits with no real logic change.
phase1_batch3_fresh_github_note: Set B fresh-GitHub mining pass (executed inline, no sub-fork): cloned 17 of 22 targeted small/pure Python libraries (docopt, fire2, argh, python-dotenv, send2trash, watchdog, pyfiglet, art, emoji, python-slugify, num2words, bidict, python-frozendict, multidict, orderedmultidict, python-sortedcollections, python-Levenshtein, jellyfish -- 5 targets failed to clone, wrong org/repo name).
